title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Production traffic showed intermittent tail-latency spikes during sustained multi-tenant workloads. Root cause analysis pointed to unfair queueing in the continuous batcher scheduler where long-running, high-token requests could starve smaller high-priority requests. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and add configurable timeouts/aging for enqueued work.

What this PR changes: 1) Introduces per-tenant deficit tokens and a weighted round-robin admission path to ensure tenants with sparse high-priority requests are served promptly. 2) Adds an aging heuristic (max_age_ms) that increases effective priority of enqueued requests proportionally to wait time to avoid starvation. 3) Implements per-request enqueue timeouts and a multilevel fallback policy: if a request exceeds enqueue timeout, it is either routed to a lower-cost fast-path model variant (if compatible) or rejected with a clear error for upstream retry. 4) Adds hysteresis to queue-length based batching thresholds to avoid oscillation during bursts. 5) Exposes new tuning knobs via continuous_batcher config and runtime feature-flag gating for gradual rollout. 6) Metrics/tracing: added queue_wait_ms histogram, per-tenant queue_length gauge, starvation_count counter, enqueue_timeout counter, and tracing spans for queue->dispatch transitions. 7) Integration with KV cache: scheduler now signals expected request lifespan to the KV cache manager so that short-lived requests do not evict long-lived cached prefixes unexpectedly.

Files touched are intentionally small and focused: scheduler core, tests, config, metrics plumbing, and onboarding doc. No model execution kernels were modified in this change, but changes surface kernel scheduling hints via the scheduler->executor interface.

Testing and benchmarks: - Unit tests: added deterministic scheduler tests covering aging and weighted admission. - Integration: perf-canary run with 1k qps mixed-tenancy workload and synthetic adversarial long-run requests. Results: 95th percentile latency improved by ~18% for high-priority requests under mixed load; median latency unchanged. Starvation incidents dropped to 0 in the canary window. - CI: full build/test/lint passed; one flaky benchmark was re-run and stabilized.

Rollout plan: Feature gated. Stage 1: internal canary in perf-canary and staging clusters (this PR). Stage 2: gradual rollout to 10% of production serving nodes with telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds. Stage 3: 100% rollout if no regressions after 72h per cohort. Backout: disable feature flag or revert to previous config quickly; an automated fallback policy will route affected requests to registered model variants.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration benchmark run - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated - [x] Config and defaults documented - [x] Rollout plan and feature flag included

Related: ENG-4821 (scheduler fairness), ENG-4930 (continuous-batcher follow-ups), SUP-784 (customer incident that motivated timeouts).
